comments: Unusual high-frequency tonal noise pattern from passing boat, plus a couple jingles. This was a high-wind day in Puget Sound...

Unusual high-frequency tonal noise pattern from passing boat, intense at first and then fainter, intermittently. This was a high-wind day in Puget Sound which may explain some of the broadband noise at frequencies below the tonal noise.

Unusual high-frequency tonal noise pattern (likely from a passing boat). In this clip it is nearly continuous with some dramatic modulations. This was a high-wind day in Puget Sound... and some sections have lower-frequency tones and modulations that sound a bit like wind whistling -- maybe when gusts blow through under the pier above the hydrophone?
Interesting sound at 4 seconds (possible humpback?) but otherwise there's mostly a mid-frequency hiss. Not sure what caused the false positives!
Variable amplitude in 60Hz hum, plus some crackling.
No ocean signal. Hydrophone may have been damaged during tonight's wind storm...
No ocean signal. Electrical noise comes and goes. Hydrophone may have been damaged during tonight's wind storm...
Faint SRKW calls, almost all S44s, through a bit of AM radio interference and boat noise.
Faint calls, some clicks, quiet background
Very faint calls, mostly quiet background with some scraping sounds
All detections seem to have been caused by jingling sounds. We still don't know the source of these but they've occurred at multiple locations...
High call rate, clearly audible despite noise from ferry.
Diverse call types including S01, S04, S07, S10 and possible percussives (near 45s) with low ambient noise (just sloshing sounds).
Minimal signals in first 30 sec, then clear S01s, aberrant calls, S16, possible S03s and shortened S07s?

Four very clear Bigg's calls possibly from animal getting closer in range (increased amplitude of last call) and wonderful reverberations after each of the first 3. There are also faint tonal signals, likely calls of a more distant individual or group.
Calls barely audible over loud ship noise
Subtle tonal structure in minimal vessel noise. Not sure what caused these false positive detections.
Moderate calls, loud boat noise, some clicks
Faint to moderate calls, some clicks, moderate boat nose
Not sure what caused these false positives. All I hear is very faint, subtle crackling with a few snaps...

Faint calls and moderate noise (DB). Only a few calls in the first half; 2nd half no signals. Labeling J pod based on ON having them in Possession Triangle at this time with L pod still up near Penn Cove. (SV).
High frequency intermittent screeching and squeaks (from railroad car wheels?)
Faint to moderate calls and ambient noise
Good calls, rain contributing to ambient noise
Jingling and clinking with some waves and low frequency short rumbles.
High call rate (mostly S02 starts) at moderate SNR

Not sure what caused false positives in this low ambient noise clip. Could be faint tonal aspects of ship noise, (from a tug?) but some seem associated with local snaps (mimicking echolocation clicks that may have inadvertently been in training data?). The final prediction may be associated with a fish grunt.
Moderate calls, Lord of water nose, a little radio
Impressive performance of the model, detecting almost all of the calls, despite intense low frequency noise from a passing train, as well as tonal train-whistles.
A few clear S01s at the end, all detected successfully, but a few faint calls missed earlier, including a S07 call.
Clear S03 calls with little background noise, other than a bit of radio interference.
Moderately clear calls in the detections, plus a few audible calls not detected including a faint S07 near the end.
J pod calls clear through a small amount of radio interference.
Clear calls, relatively low background noise. S44 and S42 at beginning, then two S01s, then more S42s, S01s, and possibly a couple fainter S07s.
Clear calls from J pod thru radio interference
Faint calls, ship nose at beginning

At first I thought it might be some sort of weird HF calls nearly continuous from SRKWs, but I think this may be a drone flying above the hydrophone or something that sounds similar to a drone in the ocean.
First time I've heard the jingle at North San Juan Channel!
More jingles, and a few clank-like short ones that have harmonics or overtones to much higher frequencies.
Faint mid-frequency chirps seem to have caused first couple false positives. Not sure about the latter 3...
Moderate to strong calls, moderate ambient noise, neat echoes
faint calls, cable noise and wave noise
J pod calls during NB travel per WSSJI & ON.
Unusual harmonic signal with many harmonics all inaudible to me.  Not biophony, for sure.
Jingling bell or key sounds with power peaks near 5.0, 5.6, and 9.5kHz. The source is unkown, currently.
Relatively high frequency tonal noise from a boat seems to have caused these false positives, possibly where the tone modulated the most during the 60-sec clip.
Squeaks from beach camp mat attached to ladder rubbing in the waves.
Human voices and breaking wave noise
AM radio interference. False positives sometimes seem associated with individual, relatively-isolated, human words.
Human voices on AM radio and contact noise from what Joel explained are mats: "during the summer we have some floating mats clipped to the ladder which are probably making the contact noise"
Ship noise with high pitched whine
AM radio interference (music, talking) and LF contact noise.
Human voices causing false positives in contact and AM radio noise.
Human voices via am radio noise
Human voices causing false positives despite significant noise from something contacting ladder and/or hydrophone.
Tonal boat noise with some swishing and lots of contact noise.
Water sounds and swishing caused false positives. Later in clip there is tonal boat noise.
Periodic water and wave impact sounds with human voices on 4th of July in between. Sounds like element was mostly out of the water.
False positives caused by human voices on 4th of July with element out of water.
Good calls and clicks, some water slosh
Human voices audible over ship noise. Not sure if they are from humans on beach or from radio interference...
Faint calls, lots of water slosh
Good calls and clicks, high background noise
Faint calls or whistles, high ship noise
Good calls and clicks, relatively low background noise
Moderate calls and clicks, high ship noise
Faint calls mostly captured by model. Also some slow clicks from SRkWs in the last quarter of the clip.
Faint calls in lots of surface wave noise.
Four pretty clear S01 calls all captured within detections.
Water and a little vessel noise
Surging waves moving gravel likely causing clicks and snaps. Snap sequences may be confusing the AI.
SRKW calls as J pod goes NB thru Haro Strait.
A couple faint calls, loud ship noise
Strong clicks, faint calls, moderate noise (initial moderation time = 20240324-130212, DBain)
Many clear calls followed by faint calls
Wiper noise with most false positives grouped in mid-candidate and one at the end.
Faint calls, some ship noise, water noise
Many clear S01 calls with possible S10, S07, and one S16.
DB note: Faint calls, electrical noise, water slosh. SV note: no detections showing on OSX+Chrome in Details view.
S01 and other calls with some system noises.
